name: Cathedral Cove
bio: A natural sea arch connecting two white-sand beaches, reached by a scenic walk from Hahei.

name: Hot Water Beach
bio: A beach where thermal water rises through the sand, so visitors dig their own hot pools at low tide.

name: Hahei
bio: A relaxed beach village, the base for Cathedral Cove, with a marine reserve and kayaking.

name: Driving Creek Railway
bio: A narrow-gauge railway through native forest built by a potter, ending at a hilltop lookout.

name: Coromandel
bio: A historic gold-rush town of villas, arts and craft shops and boutique cafés.

name: Hamilton Gardens
bio: Themed gardens including Japanese, Italian Renaissance, Indian Char Bagh and Māori gardens beside the Waikato River.

name: Hobbiton Movie Set
bio: The preserved Shire from the Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit films, visited by guided tour among hobbit holes.

name: Waikato Museum
bio: A museum of Māori art and Waikato history and a gallery, including the waka Te Winika.

name: Hamilton Zoo
bio: A zoo with Sumatran tigers, giraffes and a walk-through aviary, set among native bush.

name: Manu Bay
bio: One of the world's longest left-hand surf breaks, easily watched from the shore.

name: Bridal Veil Falls
bio: A 55-metre waterfall reached by a short walk through bush to a viewing platform.

name: Mount Karioi
bio: An extinct volcano above Raglan, with forest tracks and views over the coast.

name: Ngarunui Beach
bio: A patrolled black-sand beach that suits learner surfers, with clear views of the Karioi peak.

name: Waitomo Glowworm Caves
bio: Limestone caves where visitors glide by boat beneath a ceiling of thousands of glowworms.

name: Ruakuri Cave
bio: A cave of spiral entrance, waterfalls and glowworms, visited on a guided walking tour.

name: Aranui Cave
bio: A dry limestone cave decorated with delicate stalactites and stalagmites.

name: Marokopa Falls
bio: A 35-metre waterfall on the Marokopa River, reached by a short bush walk.

name: Mangapohue Natural Bridge
bio: A natural limestone arch reached by an easy track beside a stream.

name: Huka Falls
bio: A thundering gorge where the Waikato River squeezes through a narrow channel and drops as a turquoise cascade.

name: Craters of the Moon
bio: A geothermal area of steaming vents and craters crossed by a boardwalk.

name: Aratiatia Rapids
bio: A gorge where the dam gates open on schedule, sending the river rushing through.

name: Orakei Korako
bio: A hidden geothermal valley reached by boat, with silica terraces and a steaming cave.

name: Taupō Bungy
bio: A 47-metre jump from a cantilevered platform over the Waikato River.
